transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today? How can I help you?

Hi. Um, well, student health actually sent me over here. They told me my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops I'm supposed to be helping with this semester. Which is really frustrating because I've been planning to volunteer with this after-school art program for middle schoolers for months. They're kind of chaotic, honestly—like, last week one of the kids got acrylic paint all over the community center floor, and it was this whole massive drama with the building manager. I had to stay like two hours late just helping scrub it out of the linoleum because the program director was totally freaking out... 

But, um, anyway. Yeah, student health says the number on the scale keeps dropping, but to me it just feels like... I don't know, it's just what naturally happens when I’m really focused and busy with everything I have going on.
Have you noticed yourself losing weight without trying, or without any changes to your diet or activity level?

Without trying? Um... no, not exactly. I mean, I definitely put effort into it. I actually plan my whole day around not really eating. Like, I'll just have coffee before I go to the studio. I'm taking this advanced ceramics class right now, and wheel throwing takes so much focus. You have to center the clay perfectly or the whole bowl just collapses into this muddy puddle, which actually happened to me on Tuesday and completely ruined my favorite vintage sweater... I had to soak it in the dorm sink for like an hour and it still has a stain. 

But anyway, yeah, just coffee. And then maybe I'll have a few bites of something from the campus café later, but honestly only if people are sitting with me and watching. My roommate is always hovering lately. She just got this desk job at the campus library and suddenly acts like she's a life coach because she reads the backs of self-help books during her shift. It's so annoying. But when I do have to get something at the café to get her off my back, I totally avoid bread or anything oily. It just feels like... I don't know, like eating that kind of stuff would instantly undo all the control I’ve worked so hard for.
Do you find yourself very fearful of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might tell you that you're already underweight?

Yeah, I mean... honestly, the idea of gaining even a single pound just makes me completely panic. Like, yesterday my roommate—the library one I was just telling you about—she decided to surprise me by cooking dinner. She made this huge pasta dish she found from some TikTok influencer who does these cozy fall meals. Which, by the way, is just an excuse to use a ridiculous amount of heavy cream and cheese. She is so obsessed with TikTok right now, she literally spent three hours scrolling last night instead of studying for her biology midterm. I have no idea how she's passing that class. Her professor is Dr. Henderson, the guy who literally locks the lecture hall doors at exactly 9:00 AM. If you're one minute late, you're locked out in the hallway. My friend Sarah got locked out twice last week and she was in tears... 

But um, what was I... right, the dinner. Yeah, just the thought of sitting down and eating a normal dinner like that, or eating anything with butter in it... it terrifies me. I just feel like if I did that, everyone would instantly be able to look at me and see that I've completely lost all my discipline.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself exercise a lot, skip meals, or do anything else to try to 'undo' or compensate for the food you ate?

Um, I mean, no, not really. I don't really do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up or take pills or anything. I just... I mostly just stick to my routine, you know? Like, my routine is really important to me. I have to wake up at exactly 6:00 AM every day so I can get to the studio before anyone else is there. It's so peaceful in the morning. The light comes through these huge industrial windows, and it's just me and the clay. 

Although, the heating in that building is completely broken. It's freezing in there right now. They've been saying they're going to fix it since October, but facilities management at this school is a total joke. My friend Liam—he's in my ceramics class—he actually brought in this tiny space heater last week, but it blew a fuse and knocked out the power for the whole floor. The professor was so mad because someone was in the middle of firing the kiln and it completely messed up the temperature cycle. Liam felt so bad, he actually bought the professor a coffee the next day to apologize, but it was from that place off-campus that always burns their espresso beans, so I don't think it helped much... 

But yeah, anyway. No, I don't really do anything to 'undo' eating. I just... I just try not to eat the things I shouldn't in the first place.
